349645.title: The 6-coupled-choosability conjecture for planar partial 3-trees
349645.statement:
A **planar partial 3-tree** is a graph that is a subgraph of an Apollonian network, where an Apollonian network is obtained recursively by starting with a triangle and stellating non-outer triangular faces. Here, stellating a face means inserting a new vertex inside it and joining that vertex to all three vertices of the face.

**Planar partial 3-tree conjecture.** Every planar partial 3-tree is 6-coupled-choosable.

The conjecture is motivated by determining the coupled choosability number of planar partial 3-trees. The paper establishes that every wheel graph is 5-coupled-choosable, while its construction shows that wheels with at least seven spokes need not be 4-coupled-choosable; the stated 6-coupled-choosability claim for all planar partial 3-trees remains open.

349656.title: P-position semilinearity conjecture for Exact Slow $k$-Nim
349656.statement: Let ${\sc Nim}^1_{n,=k}$ be the impartial game on nonnegative integer vectors in which a move decreases exactly $k$ coordinates by one. A position from which the previous player can force a win is called a **P-position**. A set of integer vectors is **semilinear** if it can be expressed in Presburger arithmetic, equivalently as a finite union of solution sets of systems of linear inequalities and congruences. **Semilinearity conjecture.** For any $n$ and $k$, the P-positions of ${\sc Nim}^1_{n,=k}$ form a semilinear set. The explicit characterization for ${\sc Nim}^1_{6,=2}$ gives a polynomial-time decision procedure, motivating the conjecture for all values of $n$ and $k$.

349708.title: Meagher–Spiga multipartite derangement graph conjecture
349708.statement:
Let $n$ be an even positive integer that is not a power of $2$. A transitive permutation group of degree $n$ has a **complete multipartite derangement graph** if its derangement graph is complete multipartite.

**Multipartite derangement graph conjecture.** If $n$ is even but not a power of $2$, then there is a transitive group $G$ of degree $n$ such that its derangement graph is a complete multipartite graph with $n/2$ parts.

This conjecture concerns the existence of transitive groups whose derangement graphs have the specified multipartite structure. The paper constructs infinite families supporting it, including groups of degree $4\ell$ with complete $2\ell$-partite derangement graphs for odd $\ell$, but the assertion for every even $n$ that is not a power of $2$ remains open.

349881.title: Conjecture on lengths of extremal rational curves
349881.statement:
Let $(X,\Delta)$ be the dlt pair and setup of Theorem 1.6(iii), with a contraction morphism $iphi_{R_j}$ associated to a $(K_X+Delta)$-negative extremal ray $R_j$, and suppose $iphi_{R_j}\colon U_j\to iphi_{R_j}(U_j)$ is proper. Define 
$$
d_j=\min_E\dim E,
$$
 where $E$ ranges over positive-dimensional irreducible components of $(iphi_{R_j}|_{U_j})^{-1}(P)$ for all $P\in iphi_{R_j}(U_j)$. **Conjecture on lengths of extremal rational curves.** There exists a possibly singular rational curve $C_j\subset U_j$ spanning $R_j$ in $N_1(X/S)$ and satisfying 
$$
0<-omega\cdot C_j\leq d_j+1.
$$
 This is presented as a conjectural length bound for extremal rational curves, related to the cited question in Matsuki; no resolution is specified in the source.

350049.title: Faudree–Rousseau–Sheehan's strongly regular graph conjecture
350049.statement:
A **strongly regular graph** $srg(\nu,k,\lambda,\mu)$ is a graph of order $\nu$ that is $k$-regular, with every adjacent pair having $\lambda$ common neighbors and every nonadjacent pair having $\mu$ common neighbors. Define

$$
s=k-\lambda-1,\qquad t=k-\mu.
$$

**Faudree–Rousseau–Sheehan's conjecture.** There exists a constant $c\ge2$ such that for every strongly regular graph $srg(\nu,k,\lambda,\mu)$,

$$
2(s+t)-\nu\le c.
$$

The paper says this conjecture is closely related to the linear upper-bound conjecture for book Ramsey numbers and places it in the context of strongly regular graphs, which provide lower bounds for related Ramsey numbers. No resolution is given in the supplied source.

350069.title: Carousel extremal tournament conjecture for inducibility of $C_k$
350069.statement: Let $C_k$ be the $k$-vertex carousel tournament, and let $C_n$ be the carousel tournament on $n$ vertices. For a tournament $T$, write $I(C_k,T)$ for the number of induced copies of $C_k$ in $T$. **Carousel extremal tournament conjecture.** For all $k\ge 5$ and $n\ge k$, the unique $n$-vertex tournaments maximizing $I(C_k,T)$ are the tournaments $C_n$. This would extend the proved $C_4$ extremal result and the flag-algebra evidence for $C_5$, $C_6$, $C_7$, and $C_8$; the conjecture remains open in general.

350318.title: Wiener–eccentricity monotonicity conjecture under edge contraction
350318.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with at least three vertices, and let $e$ be an edge of $G$. Write $G.e$ for the graph obtained by contracting $e$. The Wiener index is

$$
W(G)=\sum_{\{u,v\}\subset V(G)}d_G(u,v),
$$

and the eccentricity of $G$ is

$$
\varepsilon(G)=\sum_{u\in V(G)}\varepsilon_G(u).
$$

**Wiener–eccentricity monotonicity conjecture.** For every such edge $e$,

$$
W(G.e)-\varepsilon(G.e)\leq W(G)-\varepsilon(G).
$$

The conjecture asserts that contracting an edge cannot increase the difference between the Wiener index and total eccentricity. The source notes that the claim was proved when $e$ is a bridge; its general status is not specified in the supplied text.

350439.title: The matroid lift construction conjecture
350439.statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid. A **lift** of $M$ is a matroid obtained from $M$ by increasing its rank while preserving the relevant lift relation. Let $\mathcal{C}(M)$ denote the set of circuits of $M$, and let $N$ be a matroid on $\mathcal{C}(M)$ satisfying the construction condition $(*)$. The construction produces a lift $M^N$ of $M$. **The matroid lift construction conjecture.** For every lift $K$ of $M$, there is a matroid $N$ on the circuits of $M$ satisfying $(*)$ such that

$$
K\cong M^N.
$$

This conjecture asserts that the generalized matroid construction captures every lift, extending Brylawski's result for elementary lifts. It is stated as open, although it is known in some low-corank and representable cases.

350518.title: Robust connectivity conjecture for planar triangulations
350518.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar triangulation, and let $\kappa_\rho(G)$ denote its robust connectivity. **Planar triangulation robust connectivity conjecture.**

$$
\kappa_\rho(G) \geq \frac{1}{2}.
$$

Planar triangulations on at least four vertices are $3$-connected, and the source has already established bounds for planar $3$-connected graphs. The conjecture asks whether the stronger lower bound $1/2$ holds for every planar triangulation; its resolution is not supplied here.

350624.title: The fractional transversal game inequality conjecture
350624.statement:
Let $H$ be a finite hypergraph, and let $\tau_g(H)$ denote its ordinary transversal game number and $\tau_g^*(H)$ its fractional transversal game number. **Fractional transversal game inequality conjecture.** For every hypergraph $H$, 

$$
\tau_g^*(H)\leq\tau_g(H).
$$

This is stated as a weaker consequence of the preceding integer-move conjecture. The paper presents it as an open problem; it asserts that allowing fractional moves should not increase the game value.

$$
\text{$k$-Inversion is NP-complete for all positive integers }k.
$$

The paper notes that this would follow from the dijoin additivity conjecture together with its proof that $1$-Inversion is NP-complete. Thus the assertion remains conditional on the unresolved dijoin conjecture.

351078.title: Conjecture on packing families of bounded-degree trees with non-spanning members
351078.statement:
Let a **tree family** be a family $(T_s)_{s\in[N]}$ of trees. **Bounded-degree tree-family packing conjecture.** There exist $\delta>0$ and $n_0\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every $n\ge n_0$, every tree family $(T_s)_{s\in[N]}$ satisfying

$$
\Delta(T_s)\le n/2\quad\text{and}\quad v(T_s)\le n\qquad\text{for all }s\in[N],
$$

$$
\delta n\le v(T_s)\le(1-\delta)n\qquad\text{for all }s\in[\delta n],
$$

and

$$
\sum_{s\in[N]}e(T_s)\le\binom{n}{2}
$$

packs into $K_n$. This is motivated by necessary constraints on general tree families, including the need for many non-spanning trees; the paper does not report a resolution of this conjecture.

351124.title: The fiberedness conjecture for cyclic tilings
351124.statement:
Let $A\oplus B=\mathbb{Z}_M$ be a tiling, where $M=\prod_{j=1}^K p_j^{n_j}$. Say that a set is $M/p_i^{\alpha_i}$-fibered in the $p_i$ direction when it has the corresponding fibered structure on that scale.

**Fiberedness conjecture.** For every $i$ there exists $1\leq\alpha_i<n_i$ such that either $A$ or $B$ is $M/p_i^{\alpha_i}$-fibered in the $p_i$ direction. In particular, if $M$ has $3$ prime factors, $\Phi_M\mid A$, and there exists a $D(M)$ grid $\Lambda$ such that $A\cap\Lambda$ is not fibered in any direction, then $B$ is fibered in all directions on some scale.

The conjecture is motivated by the role of fibering in the paper's tiling arguments and by the behavior of Szabó-type examples. The source presents it as an unresolved structural assertion.

351193.title: Cycle-rank conjecture for vertex metric dimension
351193.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. Let $L(G)$ denote the number of leaves, and let $c(G)=\left\vert E(G)\right\vert-\left\vert V(G)\right\vert+1$ be its cyclomatic number. The **cycle-rank conjecture for vertex metric dimension.**

$$
\mathrm{dim}(G)\leq L(G)+2c(G).
$$

The paper proves this bound for cactus graphs and notes that it also holds for $3$-connected graphs; its validity for all connected graphs is left as a conjecture.

351194.title: Zero-forcing cycle-rank conjecture for edge metric dimension
351194.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph. Let $Z(G)$ denote its zero forcing number, let $c(G)=\left\vert E(G)\right\vert-\left\vert V(G)\right\vert+1$ be its cyclomatic number, and let $\mathrm{edim}(G)$ denote its edge metric dimension. The **zero-forcing cycle-rank conjecture for edge metric dimension.**

$$
\mathrm{edim}(G)\leq Z(G)+c(G).
$$

This is proposed as the edge-metric counterpart of the vertex metric-dimension conjecture. The paper establishes analogous results for cactus graphs and records the bound for $3$-connected graphs, but the assertion for all connected graphs remains open.

351288.title: Martin's finite CRG conjecture for edit distance functions
351288.statement:
Let $d4d8$ be a non-trivial hereditary property, and let $d4d2(d4d8)$ be the set of CRGs avoiding its forbidden graphs. For each $p
a[0,1]$, let $g_K(p)$ denote the quadratic minimization function associated with a CRG $K$. **Martin's finite CRG conjecture.** For every $d700>0$, there is a finite subset $d4d2'\subseteqd4d2(d4d8)$ such that

$$
\operatorname{ed}_{\mathcal{H}}(p)=\min_{K\in\mathcal{K}'}g_K(p),\qquad\text{for all }p\in(\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon).
$$

This conjecture asks whether the edit distance function is determined by finitely many CRGs uniformly on every compact subinterval of $(0,1)$.

351460.title: Kaiser–Ryjáček–Král–Rosenfeld–Voss prism-Hamiltonicity conjecture for 3-connected planar graphs
351460.statement:
A **3-connected planar graph** is a planar graph that remains connected after the deletion of any set of at most two vertices. The **prism** over a graph $G$ is the Cartesian product $G \square K_2$, and $G$ is **prism-hamiltonian** when $G \square K_2$ has a Hamilton cycle.

**Kaiser–Ryjáček–Král–Rosenfeld–Voss conjecture.** Every 3-connected planar graph has a hamiltonian prism.

This conjecture asks whether every 3-connected planar graph reaches the hamiltonian-prism level in the hierarchy of spanning structures. It lies between Hamilton paths and $2$-walks; the existence of a $2$-walk is known for every 3-connected planar graph, but the hamiltonian-prism assertion remains open.

351463.title: Global convergence conjecture for fractional combinatorial Calabi flow with surgery
351463.statement: Let $(M,V,\varepsilon)$ be a marked weighted connected closed surface with $\varepsilon:V\rightarrow\{0,1\}$, and suppose there exists a PL or PH metric generated by a discrete conformal structure with combinatorial curvature $\overline{K}$. For any $s\in\mathbb{R}$ and any initial PL or PH metric on $(M,V,\varepsilon)$ generated by a discrete conformal structure, **Global convergence conjecture.** the solution of fractional combinatorial Calabi flow with surgery exists for all time and converges exponentially fast after a finite number of surgeries. This extends the known convergence results for the cases $s=0$ and $s=1$ to arbitrary real $s$; because the fractional combinatorial Calabi flow is generally not a gradient flow, finiteness of surgeries is not known in general.
